title: The Sun, Up Close
objective: After this level you can explain what powers the Sun and how dominant it is in the solar system.
summary: The Sun fuses hydrogen into helium, holds 99.8% of the solar system's mass, and is about 4.6 billion years old.

cards.headline: The Sun isn't on fire. It's doing something far stranger.
cards.body: There's no burning in the everyday sense. Deep in its core, the Sun squeezes atoms together.

cards.headline: Nuclear fusion
cards.body: At about 15 million °C, the Sun's core fuses hydrogen into helium. That fusion releases the energy that eventually reaches you as sunlight.

cards.fact: The Sun holds about 99.8% of the solar system's mass.
cards.context: Every planet, moon, asteroid and comet together makes up the remaining 0.2%. We're the crumbs.

cards.headline: Middle-aged, not old
cards.body: The Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago. That sounds ancient, but for a star like ours it's roughly the middle of its life.

cards.headline: Sun: understood
learned: Fusion turns hydrogen into helium in the core
The Sun is 99.8% of the solar system's mass

options.label: Burning gas, like a campfire
options.rationale: There's no combustion — the Sun has no oxygen fire.

options.label: Heat left over from its formation
options.rationale: Leftover heat would have run out long ago.

options.label: Reflected light from other stars
options.rationale: The Sun makes its own light.

questions.explanation: In its core, the Sun fuses hydrogen into helium, releasing enormous energy.

questions.prompt: From Level 1: what kind of object is the Sun?

options.label: A planet
options.rationale: Planets don't make their own light.

options.label: A galaxy
options.rationale: A galaxy contains billions of stars.

options.label: A nebula
options.rationale: A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust.

questions.explanation: The Sun is a star — the closest one to Earth.
